title: AI In Mathematics Challenges Academic Norms
excerpt: AI labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are rapidly advancing automated mathematical reasoning, with OpenAI claiming to have solved the Navier-Stokes...
content_html:
AI labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are rapidly advancing automated mathematical reasoning, with OpenAI claiming to have solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. At the Heidelberg Laureate Forum, mathematicians including Fields Medalists Peter Scholze and Geordie Williamson criticized OpenAI's conduct around the announcement as coercive and PR-driven, while raising broader concerns about how AI is reshaping mathematical research, hiring, education, and the financial burden on researchers who feel pressured to pay for LLM subscriptions to keep pace with peers.

Questions this post answers

Did OpenAI actually solve the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem?

OpenAI announced it had solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, but the claim remains unverified by the mathematics community. Fields Medalist Jacob Tsimerman called the achievement seemingly definitive, while others, including Peter Scholze, suggested the announcement was more a PR stunt than a validated breakthrough. Follow daily.dev for updates as the mathematics community verifies or disputes major AI research claims.

Why are mathematicians upset with OpenAI over its math problem announcements?

Mathematicians including Fields Medalists Peter Scholze and Geordie Williamson criticized OpenAI for behaving poorly and disrupting disciplinary norms. Mathematician Tristan Buckmaster claimed OpenAI sent correspondence to a colleague that appeared coercive, censorious, and even threatening while he was independently working on the same Navier-Stokes problem with Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge. Researchers navigating AI labs encroaching on their work can track this drama on daily.dev.

Which Millennium Prize Problem might AI companies solve next after Navier-Stokes?

Anthropic has used an unreleased version of Claude to attempt the Riemann hypothesis, making progress on a related problem but not solving the main conjecture as of August. OpenAI is reportedly focusing its efforts on the Hodge conjecture, another of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, following its Navier-Stokes claim. daily.dev readers tracking the AI-versus-mathematics race can follow which problem falls next.
